claims.text: The initial (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy is a solid solution.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can introduce a heterogeneous grain structure into the alloy.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can introduce 3D twin architectures into the alloy.
The intervention will alter the grain-boundary and twin-boundary density.
The heterogeneous grain structure and 3D twins will provide additional pathways for stress relaxation.
The heterogeneous grain structure and 3D twins will improve the alloy's ability to absorb and distribute applied loads.
Stress relaxation and improved load distribution will increase resistance to cracking.
The intervention will increase ultimate tensile strength by 25% relative to the untreated alloy.
The intervention will preserve caloric performance as measured by adiabatic temperature change.
The proposed response applies over magnetic fields from 0 to 5 T.
The proposed response applies over pressure fields from 0 to 100 MPa.
The proposed response applies from 250 to 350 K.
The proposed integrity improvement applies under uniaxial tensile loading.
A boundary operating point is 5 T, 100 MPa, 350 K, and 500 MPa tensile loading.
The magnitude of the integrity improvement may depend on processing conditions and the resulting microstructure.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 25% integrity increase, but the falsification rule rejects only increases below 10%; therefore, an observed increase of 10% to less than 25% would fail the quantitative prediction without falsifying the stated hypothesis.
